CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal testing - Advanced maternal age (37 years)

SPECIMEN TYPE
Amniotic fluid

TEST PERFORMED
Conventional cytogenetic analysis (G-banded karyotype)

PREVIOUS TESTING
Rapid PCR analysis completed (see separate report)

METHODOLOGY
Amniotic fluid cells were cultured using standard in situ culture techniques. Metaphase chromosomes were harvested and G-banded using trypsin-Giemsa staining. A minimum of 20 metaphase cells were analyzed at a resolution of 400-550 bands. Karyotypes were described according to the International System for Human Cytogenomic Nomenclature (ISCN 2020).

RESULT
Karyotype: 46,XX

INTERPRETATION
Normal female karyotype. No numerical or structural chromosomal abnormalities were detected at the resolution of this analysis. The quality of the preparation was sufficient to exclude trisomy 21 (Down syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), and other major chromosomal abnormalities.

This result indicates a chromosomally normal female fetus. The normal chromosomal complement excludes major chromosomal causes of intellectual disability and birth defects detectable by conventional karyotyping.

LIMITATIONS
Conventional karyotyping cannot detect:
- Chromosomal abnormalities smaller than approximately 5-10 Mb
- Low-level mosaicism (<10-20%)
- Single gene disorders
- Uniparental disomy
- Methylation abnormalities

For detection of submicroscopic chromosomal imbalances, chromosomal microarray analysis may be considered.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD

Laboratory Accreditation: CAP #[redacted ID], CLIA #[redacted ID]
